paragraphs.text: Restart the DeepSeek Harness desktop app and its host process from a session header button or the sy
stem tray (Windows).
# dsh-tray-restart
Restart the DeepSeek Harness desktop app — the Electron shell **and** the Host process it runs — wit
hout quitting by hand.
A restart button in the session header, plus a Windows tray icon with the same action. Other plugins
, skins, and settings are reloaded on the way up.
> **Windows only.** The plugin lives on WinForms and `taskkill`; on any other platform it does nothi
.** The plugin lives on WinForms and `taskkill`; on any other platform it does nothing and logs why.
## What you get

- **Header button** — a small restart icon in the top-right utilities row of every session.
- **Tray
icon** — right-click for `Restart DSH (app + host)` / `Open DeepSeek Harness` / `Quit tray icon`. L

eft-click opens the app.
- **One action** — both paths kill the whole process tree (`taskkill /T /F`
), wait for it to exit, clear a stale profile lock if the previous run left one, and start the app a
it for it to exit, clear a stale profile lock if the previous run left one, and start the app again.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness desktop app, Windows 10 or 11.
- Nothing else. No build step, no dependencies.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **quit the app completely and reopen it once** — client bundles and the host rows are collected
at startup, so a page refresh is not enough.
After that first restart the plugin maintains itself: the header button is there, and the tray icon
appears on every launch.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The tray icon disappears with the next app restart (or quit it from its own menu).
## How it works
| Piece | What it does |
| `index.js` (Host) | Registers `GET /dsh-tray-restart/status` and `POST /dsh-tray-restart/restart`

on the web server, and starts the tray helper. |
| `client.js` (Web UI) | Renders the header button

into `conversation.session.header.utilities`. |
| `assets/tray.ps1` | WinForms `NotifyIcon`, polls t

he shell process so it disappears when the app does. |
| `assets/launch-*.ps1` | Start the tray or t

he restart helper through WMI (`Win32_Process.Create`) — see below. |
| `assets/restart.ps1` | Kill
the shell (and its process tree), wait, clear `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/lock`, relaunch the executa
ell (and its process tree), wait, clear `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/lock`, relaunch the executable. |
Two implementation details worth knowing if you fork this:
1. **The helper must be started outside the app's process tree.** The Host runs inside a Job object
that restricts USER handles, so a child process created with a normal `spawn`/`Start-Process` builds
its `NotifyIcon` without error but never appears in the notification area. Processes created throug
h `Win32_Process.Create` are parented to `WmiPrvSE` instead and register fine. The restart helper go
es through the same path for the same reason — and it must, because it kills the app's process tree

and would otherwise kill itself first.
2. **`ctx.get('webServer')` is `undefined` during a plugin's
`apply`.** The web server starts after plugin rows load. Route registration therefore waits with `ct
x.inject(['webServer'], …)`; the tray start is independent and must not `return` early.
Restarting from here is equivalent to quitting the app from its menu and launching it again — nothin
g is kept in memory across the restart.
